request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The ROLLUP and TOTALS audit lines are in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works.** The front end works out the claimed and due-total figures from the raw data, and the server didn't compute them anywhere. So I added a small `rollup` package on the server (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`):

- **`Rollup`** works out the sheet's figures the same way the screen does: each person's claimed amount and due-total, plus the two sheet totals. A due-total is `n/a` when there's no rate today and no figure, and `n/a` is left out of the sheet total.
- **`SnapshotRollup`** is a new first step in every write. It records the figures before the change and writes nothing.
- **`AuditRollup`** runs after the change's own audit line. It works the figures out again and writes:
  - one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order they were added (someone who didn't exist before counts as moved);
  - then a `TOTALS` line if either sheet total moved.

**Where it applies.** The two steps are added to all 8 write endpoints: today, add/edit person, set rate, add/edit claim, claim status change and statement. Changing today gets only the rollup lines, with no line of its own. A change that moves no figure writes no rollup lines.

**Two things to know:**
- The spec writes the person as `person=<name>`, not `name=<name>` as the request text says. I followed the spec, since that's what the test checks.
- The figure rules now exist twice: once on the server for the audit, and once in the front end (`features/rates/due.slot.tsx`) for what's shown on screen. If one changes, the other has to be changed to match.

No front-end changes were needed.
